citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the SVD-entropy, Petrosian, Renyi, Tsallis, dispersion, fuzzy and increment entropy cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::slopeEntropy(dimension=3, thresholds=c(0.1,45)): turn each first difference into the slope angle atan(dx) in degrees, map to one of 5 symbols by the two angle thresholds (flat within +/-0.1 deg, gentle up to +/-45 deg, steep beyond), embed into length-(m-1) slope patterns and take their Shannon entropy. The reference re-computes it with NeuroKit2 entropy_slope across the embedding dimension, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the other EEG complexity cases). Slope entropy (Cuesta-Frau 2019) is a symbolic complexity measure on the SLOPES between successive samples: each first difference becomes the angle atan(dx) (degrees), mapped to 5 symbols (steep/gentle/flat, up/down) by two angle thresholds, and SlopEn is the Shannon entropy of the length-(m-1) slope patterns. slopeEntropy is a NEW op completing the discrete-symbolic complexity trio (NCDF-dispersion / increment-magnitude / slope-angle). It reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_slope BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~9e-16) across the embedding dimension. On real eyes-closed POz EEG the signal realizes 18 of the 25 (=5^(m-1)) possible slope patterns at m=3. Unlike the normalized entropies (increment/fuzzy, which decrease with m), SlopEn is an UNNORMALIZED Shannon over length-(m-1) patterns, so it INCREASES with dimension (1.26 -> 2.43 -> 3.57) -- more/longer patterns carry more entropy. HONEST: the value depends on (dimension, thresholds)=NeuroKit2 defaults; the reproducible content is the bit-exact family and the pattern structure, not an absolute constant.
